title: Ops Snapshot: Decision Radar mini-deck (WIP)
content:
Slide 1 — Opening (30s): Ops Snapshot + One-line
- Title: "Ops Snapshot: Decision Radar"
- 30s elevator (for platform/infra buyers):
  "Redwood Inference gives your engineering org predictable latency and unit economics for LLM features — and a clear ops playbook so product teams don’t hit reliability surprises during pilot-to-scale. We handle model fallbacks, routing, and autoscaling so your SREs keep SLAs while product teams ship quickly."
- Why this deck: 2-min primer sellers can use in discovery + a 1-page decision radar for pilots and canaries.

Slide 2 — Qualification Radar (1 min): quick signals to qualify pilot fit
- Focus buyer profile: Platform/Infra, Integration Architect, or ML Platform lead.
- 6 radial signals (binary/graded):
  1) Latency SLO <= 200ms for UI: yes/no/partial
  2) Predictable throughput (peak RPS known): yes/no/partial
  3) Data isolation/regulatory needs: none / moderate / strict
  4) Willingness to run a private deployment: low / medium / high
  5) Tolerance for model quality variance: low / medium / high
  6) Budget cadence (commit vs pay-as-you-go): commit / iod / ad-hoc
- Quick seller action: If 4+ signals are medium/high -> propose 6-week pilot with dedicated capacity. If legal/regulatory = strict -> fast-track private-deploy checklist.

Slide 3 — Pilot types & quick win mapping (1 min):
- Light pilot (fast POC): Hosted API, short prompt set, focus metric = perceived latency, success = <200ms p95 and stable UX.
- Throughput pilot (scale validation): Dedicated capacity, synthetic load, measure tokens/sec and OOM/resilience.
- Regulated pilot (security): Private/VPC, deploy minimal private control plane + KMS, validate audit logs and egress.
- Buyer-facing snippet: "We recommend a two-track POC: UX-driven hosted proof to demo value in 2 weeks, and a parallel smoke test on Dedicated/Private to validate production constraints."

Slide 4 — Canary & fallback decision grid (operational cheat sheet):
- Axis: Cost sensitivity vs Availability requirement.
- Cells and example playbooks:
  High availability / High cost sensitivity -> Canary on dedicated + async fallback to cached responses; auto-scale with conservative burst policy.
  High availability / Low cost sensitivity -> Reserve dedicated capacity + regional redundancy + synchronous fallbacks to higher-cost model variants.
  Low availability / High cost sensitivity -> Hosted with aggressive prefix caching and batched inference.
  Low availability / Low cost sensitivity -> Experiment with cheaper quantized variants and aggressive rate limits.
- Auto-fallback rules (seller snippet):
  "If p95 latency > SLA or error rate spike > 2% for 3 consecutive min, route to fallback model variant X for 10m and alert SRE runbook A."

Slide 5 — Pilot success metrics & escalation (1 slide):
- Primary metrics (choose 3): UX p95 latency, token cost per successful request, correctness/QA score on safety prompt set.
- Secondary: error rates, cache hit ratio, autoscale latency.
- Escalation path (concise): SE -> Field SRE -> Solutions Eng -> Eng on-call; include contact shorthand and expected SLA to respond (15min initial ack).

Appendix A — Seller scripts & objection responses (notes):
- Objection: "Your costs look high compared to raw GPU providers."
  Response: "We optimize unit economics at the serving layer — batching, KV/prefix caching, and intelligent routing reduce cost per useful token and you avoid building/owning the reliability/ops stack. We can show a before/after runbook for your real traffic profile."
- Objection: "We can’t expose data to hosted APIs."
  Response: "We offer private deployments with customer-managed networking plus KMS/HSM integration. Timeline for a pilot typically 4–8 weeks depending on procurement; we have a checklist to accelerate security review."
- Quick snippets to open an ops call: 
  1) "Tell me about a recent incident where model latency impacted users — what did you do to mitigate?"
  2) "How do you currently measure and budget per-token cost for LLM features?"
  3) "If we could guarantee a fallback pathway for degraded capacity, would you be open to a short hosted prove-out?"

Appendix B — One-page pilot checklist (seller copy):
- Pilot objective: 
- Success metrics (3): 
- Data security level: 
- Required infra access (yes/no): 
- Duration: 2 / 4 / 6 weeks
- Runbook owner (name/email): 
- Next step: kickoff call + initial traffic sample + security pre-check link

Notes to self / TODO:
- Validate regional latency thresholds and autoscale policies for EU pilot accounts.
- Add canned Grafana view links and a one-click cost simulation for reserved vs burst.
- Confirm legal checklist items for private pilot (SLA template link).

Speaker guidance: keep it to a 3-slide demo + 1-minute qualification radar in discovery. This file is the working mini-deck sellers should carry in their browser as a 2-minute ops-focused play.
